risks.title: Single architecture and code owner has no recorded backup
risks.trigger: The primary owner is unavailable or authors a high-risk change requiring independent review.
risks.mitigation: Assign named primary and backup owners by platform/data, API/delivery and product/contracts boundaries; require an external reviewer for security and production releases until teams exist.

risks.title: Replit source rebuild is not a measured live artifact promotion
risks.trigger: A deployment is described as running the byte-identical GitHub candidate without a provider-measured digest.
risks.mitigation: Retain exact source snapshot, provider build and immutable deployment IDs; keep runtimeIdentityEvidence environment-declared and liveArtifactDigestVerified false until measured evidence exists.

risks.title: In-process schedules can duplicate across autoscale replicas
risks.trigger: VALO_INPROCESS_SCHEDULES is enabled while more than one application replica may run.
risks.mitigation: Keep schedules off by default; before opt-in, prove a single active scheduler or add job-specific distributed exclusion and idempotency with retained duplicate-effect tests.

risks.title: Durable worker and declared schedules lack production activation evidence
risks.trigger: Operations depend on an unmounted worker or a source-declared but not-installed schedule.
risks.mitigation: Preserve activation gates, assign workload identities, install only eligible schedules, and retain platform IDs, first/full-cycle receipts, last-success signals, alerts and disable procedures.

risks.title: Desired repository and environment protection may differ from live GitHub state
risks.trigger: A repository policy file or passing governance test is treated as proof that live rulesets or environment reviewers are applied.
risks.mitigation: Apply the desired branch/environment policy through GitHub administration and retain a live export or API attestation in the private operations record for every review.

risks.title: Route mount semantics can drift beyond automated contract and policy-ID reconciliation
risks.trigger: A route is mounted or moved under different middleware semantics even though its OpenAPI operation, prefix default and runtime high-risk policy identifier still reconcile.
risks.mitigation: Keep verifier enforcement for OpenAPI coverage, exact runtime project-route IDs and high-risk controls; review app.ts/routes/index.ts mount order and negative near-match tests as executable truth until mount semantics are parsed automatically.

risks.title: Current, deployed and target architecture narratives can diverge
risks.trigger: A target diagram or historical acceptance record is read as current deployed evidence.
risks.mitigation: Maintain dated current, deployed, verified and target labels; link the guidebook to source catalogues; supersede stale claims and run architecture freshness/link checks.

risks.title: Clerk proxy availability and host configuration are an authentication dependency
risks.trigger: Allowed origins, proxy headers, Clerk keys or provider availability prevent valid session verification.
risks.mitigation: Keep a fixed upstream and exact host allowlist, fail closed on unknown hosts, verify production provider approval/key custody, and retain identity outage smoke evidence.

risks.title: Exact database attestation can trade availability for security correctness
risks.trigger: An intended migration changes an attested role, policy, trigger, function or privilege without synchronized source/test updates.
risks.mitigation: Treat attestation failure as a controlled startup stop; rehearse migrations against production-shaped PostgreSQL and update migration, exact catalogue and tests in one reviewed change.

risks.title: Package assembly and final release locks can consume memory or extend contention
risks.trigger: Large governed reports/packages or concurrent exports approach process memory, request-transaction or provider latency limits.
risks.mitigation: Keep deployment byte ceilings and bounded in-memory preassembly; the current shared resource boundary deliberately holds the project advisory lock across assembly to preserve the global project-before-membership order. Load-test deadline peaks, monitor duration/memory, and require a full lock-order redesign plus database race evidence before shortening that window or introducing streaming.

risks.title: Alert delivery, backup creation and audit anchoring remain externally disconnected
risks.trigger: Source alert/validator definitions are relied on without provider capture, delivery receipts, immutable anchor or restore evidence.
risks.mitigation: Connect approved providers, independently pin evidence digests, prove paging and full-cycle schedules, and complete isolated restore and anchor-reconciliation drills before GA claims.

risks.title: API domain remains a coarse internal boundary with large hotspots
risks.trigger: Delivery, intelligence, retention, commercial or communication changes create cross-domain imports or make transactional hotspots harder to review safely.
risks.mitigation: Enforce the current edge-to-lib direction and line-budget exceptions now; introduce finer domain dependency rules only with measured change pressure and ownership, preserving transaction protocols during extraction.

risks.title: Peak-load and accessibility service measures are not yet calibrated with production evidence
risks.trigger: A release relies on an unmeasured peak/SLO or infers full accessibility from unit-level axe checks alone.
risks.mitigation: Calibrate observed peak and p95 SLO, run the 2x peak slow-provider rehearsal, and retain keyboard, screen-reader, narrow-viewport and low-bandwidth critical-task evidence before GA.
